newsitem.title: INDIA: India edible oil prices firm on truck strike.
newsitem.headline: India edible oil prices firm on truck strike.

text.p: Indian edible oil prices firmed during the week with oilseed arrivals at a standstill due to a strike by truck operators, industry officials said on Wednesday.
"Market arrivals have come to a halt as truckers had gone on a strike," Navinbhai Shah, president of the Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd, told Reuters.

Truck owners launched the strike on Tuesday in protest against a five percent service tax on road transport which Finance Minister P. Chidambaram proposed in the federal budget for the 1997/98 (April-March) financial year.
The protest has kept some 2.2 million trucks off the roads and crippled ground transport of goods.
Traders said groundnut oil rose to 35,500 rupees per tonne from 34,700 rupees last week. Palm olein oil was quoted at 28,500 rupees compared with 28,000 last week.
They said soyoil was quoted at 28,000 while sunflower (crude) oil was quoted at 25,300.

Industry officials said 200,000 tonnes of sunflower oil from Argentina and the U.S. had already arrived. "Another 100,000 tonnes of sunflower oil imports are expected to come in the next two months," Shah said.
Officials of the Central Organisation for Oil Industry and Trade expect sunflower oil imports to rise to 450,000 tonnes in 1996/97 (Nov-Oct) from 120,000 tonnes in 1995/96.
